completion_data.completion_summary: Settled the OTel <-> events.jsonl seam with a new cc_session_id join key, split skill-memory into skill-learn and skill-distill, restructured skill-distill around a shared sub-mode skeleton, and specified/landed five new or redefined telemetry-sourced /distill sub-modes (--revise, --meta, --review, --learn, --dream), growing /distill from 7 to 12 sub-modes. All 12 plan phases completed; final validation passed, including a live extension-redeploy check that found and fixed a stale-deploy defect.

memory_candidates.content: Neovim extension deploy has two independent refresh paths with different scope: deploy-headless.sh ("Load Core") only resyncs the base .claude/ core tree from lua/neotex/plugins/ai/claude/commands/picker/operations/sync.lua's load_all_globally. An already-loaded extension's own skill/context/script directories are NOT resynced by that path -- reloading an extension (e.g. after a skill split/rename in its source directory) requires calling the extension manager's own reload function, e.g. headlessly: `nvim --headless -c "lua vim.fn.confirm = function() return 1 end" -c "lua require('neotex.plugins.ai.claude.extensions').reload('EXTNAME')" -c 'qa!'`. This performs an unload-then-load against the current manifest.json, correctly removing stale directories and adding new ones. verify-deploy.sh's PASS only confirms core event-store files; it does not check per-extension skill deployment.

When splitting a large SKILL.md into two skills at a fixed line boundary, verify line-count reconciliation immediately after each cut-and-paste move (old_total == new_total_across_all_pieces) and diff each relocated block against its pre-move extraction to confirm byte-identical relocation before adding any new header/registration content. This caught the exact boundary (2941 = 1062 + 1879) and confirmed zero content loss across a later multi-step reorder (moving a 453-line block earlier in the same file) with simple sed-based extraction/reassembly plus diff, rather than relying on visual inspection of a huge file.

When a plan instructs reusing an existing sub-mode's content 'in substance unchanged' as the seed for new sub-modes (e.g. splitting an overloaded 'dream' mode into --revise and --meta), read the full existing section first to extract the exact reusable content (event ingestion, classification logic, JSON payloads) before drafting the new sections, rather than re-deriving similar-sounding content from scratch. This preserves verified-correct algorithmic detail (three-strikes thresholds, JSON schemas) and makes the 'fully contains the migrated content' verification step trivial.
